messages:
alexa: Heads up - after the RBAC change yesterday some regional services reported mTLS handshake failures when pulling certs from KMS-backed keystore. Seeing a few 500s and a spike in cert unwrap errors in logs. Anyone else?

omar: saw it. quick grep of unwrap errors: `KMS:AccessDenied` from eu-west and ap-south. US regions fine.

sam: yep, SRE alerted. stack trace points at keystore fetch path: `keystore-unwrap -> kms/unwrap` failing with iam deny. No downtime but increased latency while fallback retried.

jen: which RBAC change? I merged the service-account role tighten PR last night (rotate-keystore-access). That limited kms:Decrypt to a smaller rolebinding for a few services.

alexa: that sounds like it. We need to map which service accounts still need decrypt. Can we get a quick list from audit logs?

auditbot: AuditLog: 2026-03-20T22:10:12Z - Principal: svc-keystore-proxy@infra - Action: kms:Decrypt - Result: DENIED - Resource: projects/redwood/kms/keyrings/keystore/cryptoKeys/unwrap-key

omar: attaching snippet of the RBAC patch that likely caused it:```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: rotate-keystore-access
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: rotate-runner
  namespace: ops
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: kms-decrypt-limited
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

jen: I scoped the role to ops only - blind spot: keystore-proxy runs in infra namespace and assumes a different SA. My bad, should have included proxy SA.

alexa: ok action items: 1) temporary patch to restore decrypt for keystore-proxy SA in eu/ap; 2) add audit alerts so RBAC PRs warn on kms:Decrypt coverage gaps; 3) postmortem notes + playbook update.

omar: I'm doing (1) now. Applying patched RoleBinding to infra svc account with canary in eu-west first.

sam: for 2) can we add a CI check that queries IAM bindings and fails PRs if a role change would remove kms:Decrypt from service accounts observed in audit logs? Something like: compare current principals in last 7d KMS decrypt audit and ensure they're still bound.

jen: good idea. Rough bash prototype:```bash
# find principals that called kms:Decrypt in last 7 days
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="cloudkms.cryptoKeys.decrypt"' --limit=500 --format="value(protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail)" | sort | uniq
# then ensure each principal appears in resulting RBAC mapping
```

alexa: add that prototype as a CI job in repo infra/ci/rbac-checks. Also add a human-review gate for role scoping changes that touch KMS keys.

auditbot: RuleAdded: kms-decrypt-coverage-check registered in infra-ci with severity: warn.

deploy-bot: deploy started: namespace=infra patch=restore-keystore-proxy-decrypt eu-west canary

sam: observing eu-west canary logs - unwrap errors drop to zero and handshake success rate returns to baseline. rolling to rest of regions after 3m stable.

jen: will open follow-up PR to: 1) expand RoleBinding to include proxy SA and a test; 2) docs update in security playbooks about RBAC->KMS mapping; 3) add periodic audit that flags new principals calling kms:Decrypt (monthly).

alexa: for postmortem, capture: timeline, root cause (RBAC scope too narrow), detection (audit alerts, SRE spike), mitigation (rollback + canary), and prevention (CI check + PR human gate). keep it concise.

omar: one more ask - can we improve keystore client to surface more actionable error messages (e.g., include principal and policy hint)? currently logs only `KMS:AccessDenied`.

jen: agreed. I'll add context to unwrap errors: include `intended-principal`, `namespace`, and `key-id`. small change, low risk.

alexa: thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem and link the RBAC CI prototype. If anyone spots leftover denied principals in logs run:
```bash
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="cloudkms.cryptoKeys.decrypt" AND severity=ERROR' --limit=100 --format=json | jq '.[] | {time: .timestamp, principal: .protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, resource: .resource.labels.key}'
```

sam: copied. marking incident resolved once PRs land and infra-ci warns are green. :thumbsup:

auditbot: IncidentNote: incident_id=2026-03-20-p1, status=resolved, tags=[rbac,kms,keystore,mTLS]
